newsitem.title: JAPAN: Most Tokyo precious metals slip but palladium firm.
newsitem.headline: Most Tokyo precious metals slip but palladium firm.

text.p: Most Tokyo precious metal futures ended lower on Tuesday, depressed by the strong yen and weaker bullion prices, but palladium was mostly up amid continnued concerns about delayed Japan-Russia supply contract talks, traders said.
The spot gold February contract expired at noon at 1,396 yen, down two yen, with 5,071 lots of deliveries.

TOCOM most-active December gold ended nine yen per gram lower at 1,370 yen. "Deliveries were heavy as traders were willing to take deliveries ahead of a scheduled rise in the consumption tax in April," a trading house trader said.
In a quiet bullion market, gold was quoted at $352.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $353.00/50 in New York on Monday.
In the gold futures market, bargain-hunting buying by individual investors partly offset price losses.
Palladium prices ended mostly firmer, although profit-taking late in the day put a lid on further gains.
TOCOM February palladium expired at noon at 553 yen, with 102 lots of deliveries. TOCOM December palladium ended one yen lower at 542 per gram, after rising to 550 yen during the day.
"Trading in yen-based palladium futures is likely to continue to be volatile on lingering uncertainty over Russian supplies," one trader said.

Traders said spot palladium prices have little scope to fall as supplies in the global market remained tight, reflecting the suspension of Russian exports and buying by overseas funds in speculative moves.

Silver and platinum prices also weakened. Benchmark December silver fell 1.9 yen per 10 grams at 203.9 yen. Benchmark December platinum ended five yen per gram lower at 1,441 yen.--Tokyo Commodity Desk, -81-3-3432-7431
